cards.explanation: The answer is tastes food. Elihu says, "For the ear tests words as the mouth tastes food." (Job 34:3) So you don't just swallow every word that comes by, friends. You check it first. I never send out a batch without sampling the dough, and Elihu wants the same care with words.

The answer is False. Elihu says, "Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good." (Job 34:4) He puts himself in the group with the word "us." Nobody gets sent off to figure it out solo.

The answer is that Job is righteous, yet God has denied him justice. Elihu has Job saying he is righteous and that God has deprived him of justice (Job 34:5). Notice this is Elihu reporting Job's words, not Job speaking. Elihu is about to push back, and his next move is to say that it is far from God to do wrong (Job 34:10).

The answer is evildoers and wicked men. Elihu says Job "…keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men." (Job 34:8) That's a hard thing to say about a man, friends. Elihu says it, and the text leaves it right there.

The answer is God. Elihu says Job has said, "It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God." (Job 34:9) That's Elihu's report of what Job said. The thing Elihu says gets no profit is delighting in God.

The answer is doing wrong and acting unjustly. "Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly." (Job 34:10) Elihu has been warming up, and this is his big claim. He's saying God doing wrong is about as far away as it gets.

The answer is deeds. Elihu says, "…according to a man’s deeds He repays him…" (Job 34:11) He follows it up with, "according to a man’s ways He brings consequences." So deeds and ways are what he points to.

The answer is True. Elihu says that if God were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath, "…all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust." (Job 34:14-15) He's making a point that all life depends on God, friends. And he asks who gave God charge over the earth to begin with.

The answer is False. Elihu describes the One "who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’" (Job 34:18) Then he adds that God is not partial to princes (Job 34:19). Titles don't buy anybody a gentler word.

The answer is that they are all the work of His hands. Elihu says God is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor, and the reason he gives is, "For they are all the work of His hands." (Job 34:19) Princes and poor are made by the same hands, friends. That's why nobody gets favorites.
The answer is False. Elihu says, "There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide." (Job 34:22) He's saying no shadow is deep enough. Not even the middle of the night.

The answer is that He sets up others in their place. Elihu says God "…shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place." (Job 34:24) So the seats don't stay empty, friends. Someone else gets set there.

The answer is that they turned aside from Him. Elihu says God strikes them "…because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways." (Job 34:27) That's the reason he gives. Turning aside from Him and not caring about His ways.

The answer is the poor. Elihu says, "They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted." (Job 34:28) So the cry reached God, and He heard it, friends. The verse doesn't leave that outcry unheard.

The answer is that He watches over man and nation. Elihu says, "Yet He watches over both man and nation…" (Job 34:29) He says it right after the questions about God staying silent and hiding His face. So even then, the watching goes on.

The answer is True. Elihu says God watches over man and nation, "…that godless men should not rule or lay snares for the people." (Job 34:29-30) So the watching has a purpose attached to it in his words, friends. He's saying godless men shouldn't rule.
The answer is False. Elihu says, "You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know." (Job 34:33) The choice isn't his, because he says "not I." He puts the choosing on the "you" in that line.

The answer is that Job speaks without knowledge. Elihu says the wise men will declare, "Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight." (Job 34:35) Keep in mind this is what Elihu says they will say, friends. I think that's a hard thing to hear about anybody.

The answer is God. Elihu says Job "…adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God." (Job 34:37) That's how Elihu ends this speech, friends. And the story isn't over yet.
